children: Another factor driving consumer confidence lower in September was the surge in long-term interest rates in bond yields, says Gregory Daco, EY-Parthenon's chief economist. A confluence of factors, including inflationary concerns and rising oil prices fueled a sell-off in the bond market. Mortgage rates also hit 7% in September. "Whether you look at inflation developments or interest rate developments, they're both constraining consumer spending power and capacity," Daco tells WSJ.(jessica.coacci@wsj.com)
